points.title: 早年求学
points.description: 瓦格纳出生于莱比锡的一个小公务员家庭，幼年丧父。在莱比锡期间，他接受了初步的音乐教育，对戏剧和音乐产生了浓厚兴趣。1828年，他在莱比锡大学学习哲学，同时开始创作第一部歌剧《婚礼》。这一时期，他接触了贝多芬等作曲家的作品，深受影响，形成了自己独特的艺术理念。莱比锡的经历奠定了他后来综合艺术思想的基础，使他开始思考音乐与戏剧的结合。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Leipzig to a minor civil servant family, Wagner lost his father at a young age. During his time in Leipzig, he received basic musical education and developed a keen interest in both music and theater. In 1828, he studied philosophy at the University of Leipzig while beginning work on his first opera, 'The Wedding'. This period exposed him to the works of composers like Beethoven, profoundly influencing his artistic development. Leipzig experiences laid the foundation for his later concept of Gesamtkunstwerk (total work of art), beginning to contemplate the fusion of music and drama.

points.title: 巴黎挣扎
points.description: 1833年，瓦格纳前往巴黎寻求发展机会，但经历了艰难的时期。他担任过乐队指挥、音乐评论员，并尝试创作歌剧，但大多未能上演。在此期间，他创作了《仙女》和《禁恋》等作品，但反响平平。巴黎的挫折使他更加坚定了自己的艺术理念，同时也让他认识到传统歌剧形式的局限性。这段经历促使他开始思考歌剧改革，为后来的创作奠定了基础。1842年，当他的歌剧《黎恩济》在德累斯顿成功上演后，他终于离开了巴黎。
points.descriptionEn: In 1833, Wagner moved to Paris seeking career opportunities but faced significant hardships. He worked as a conductor, music critic, and attempted to compose operas, but most remained unperformed. During this period, he created works like 'The Fairies' and 'The Ban on Love', which received little recognition. Parisian挫折 strengthened his resolve to develop his own artistic vision and made him recognize the limitations of traditional opera forms. This experience prompted him to begin contemplating opera reform, laying groundwork for his later works. In 1842, after his opera 'Rienzi' succeeded in Dresden, he finally left Paris.

points.title: 德累斯顿辉煌
points.description: 1842年，瓦格纳的歌剧《黎恩济》在德累斯顿宫廷歌剧院大获成功，这使他获得了宫廷乐长的职位。在德累斯顿期间，他创作了《漂泊的荷兰人》、《汤豪塞》和《罗恩格林》等重要作品，这些作品展现了他独特的音乐风格和戏剧理念。瓦格纳还积极参与德累斯顿的文化生活，与当时著名的音乐家如李斯特等人保持联系。然而，1849年，他因参与德累斯顿五月起义而被迫流亡，结束了他在德累斯顿的辉煌时期。德累斯顿的经历使他的艺术风格更加成熟，也为他后来的创作积累了宝贵经验。
points.descriptionEn: In 1842, Wagner's opera 'Rienzi' achieved great success at the Dresden Court Theatre, earning him the position of Royal Kapellmeister. During his Dresden period, he created major works including 'The Flying Dutchman', 'Tannhäuser', and 'Lohengrin', showcasing his unique musical style and dramatic concepts. Wagner actively participated in Dresden's cultural life and maintained connections with prominent musicians like Liszt. However, in 1849, he was forced into exile for his involvement in the May Uprising in Dresden, ending his glorious period there. Dresden experiences matured his artistic style and accumulated valuable experience for his later works.

points.title: 流亡创作
points.description: 1849年，瓦格纳因参与德累斯顿起义被迫流亡，最终定居在瑞士苏黎世。在苏黎世的12年间，他度过了相对平静的创作生活，完成了《尼伯龙根的指环》的剧本创作，并开始构思《特里斯坦与伊索尔德》。这一时期，他撰写了《艺术与革命》、《未来的艺术作品》等重要理论著作，系统阐述了他的'总体艺术'理念。瓦格纳在苏黎世还与哲学家尼采建立了友谊，两人就艺术和哲学问题进行了深入交流。苏黎世时期是瓦格纳创作生涯的重要阶段，他的艺术理念在此期间得到系统化，为后来的歌剧创作奠定了理论基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1849, Wagner was forced into exile following his involvement in the Dresden uprising, eventually settling in Zurich, Switzerland. During his 12 years in Zurich, he experienced a relatively peaceful creative life, completing the libretto for 'The Ring of the Nibelung' and beginning to conceive 'Tristan and Isolde'. This period saw him write important theoretical works like 'Art and Revolution' and 'The Artwork of the Future', systematically articulating his concept of Gesamtkunstwerk (total work of art). Wagner also befriended philosopher Nietzsche in Zurich, engaging in deep discussions about art and philosophy. Zurich was a crucial phase in Wagner's career, where his artistic ideas were systematized, laying theoretical groundwork for his later operatic works.

points.title: 维也纳挑战
points.description: 1861年，瓦格纳获准返回德国，但主要活动中心转移到维也纳。在维也纳期间，他试图上演《特里斯坦与伊索尔德》，但遇到了巨大阻力。这部作品因其创新的音乐语言和复杂的和声结构而备受争议，直到1865年才在慕尼黑成功首演。维也纳时期，瓦格纳还与巴伐利亚国王路德维希二世建立了联系，后者成为他的重要赞助人。然而，维也纳的保守音乐环境与瓦格纳的创新理念产生了冲突，这促使他更加坚定自己的艺术道路，同时也加深了他对传统音乐体制的批判。
points.descriptionEn: In 1861, Wagner was permitted to return to Germany but primarily centered his activities in Vienna. During his Vienna period, he attempted to stage 'Tristan and Isolde' but faced significant resistance. This work was controversial due to its innovative musical language and complex harmonic structure, only premiering successfully in Munich in 1865. In Vienna, Wagner also established contact with Bavarian King Ludwig II, who became an important patron. However, Vienna's conservative musical environment conflicted with Wagner's innovative concepts, strengthening his resolve to pursue his artistic path and deepening his critique of traditional musical institutions.

points.title: 拜罗伊特巅峰
points.description: 1866年，瓦格纳移居拜罗伊特，在这里实现了他多年的梦想——创建专门上演自己作品的拜罗伊特节日剧院。1876年，首届拜罗伊特音乐节成功举办，《尼伯龙根的指环》全剧首次完整上演，标志着瓦格纳艺术生涯的巅峰。在拜罗伊特期间，他完成了《帕西法尔》等晚期作品，进一步完善了自己的音乐风格。瓦格纳还积极参与拜罗伊特音乐节的管理，确保作品按照他的意图呈现。拜罗伊特成为了瓦格纳艺术的圣地，影响深远。1883年，瓦格纳在威尼斯去世，但他的艺术遗产通过拜罗伊特音乐节得以延续，至今仍对世界音乐产生重要影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1866, Wagner moved to Bayreuth, where he realized his long-held dream of creating the Bayreuth Festival Theatre specifically for his works. In 1876, the first Bayreuth Festival successfully staged the complete 'Ring of the Nibelung' for the first time, marking the pinnacle of Wagner's career. During his Bayreuth period, he completed late works like 'Parsifal', further refining his musical style. Wagner actively participated in managing the Bayreuth Festival, ensuring his works were presented according to his intentions. Bayreuth became a sanctuary for Wagner's art with profound influence. In 1883, Wagner died in Venice, but his artistic legacy continues through the Bayreuth Festival, maintaining significant influence on world music to this day.

supporter.zh: 瓦格纳被支持者视为音乐戏剧革命的先驱，他打破了传统歌剧的束缚，创造了'总体艺术'的理念，将音乐、诗歌、戏剧和视觉艺术完美融合。他的作品如《尼伯龙根的指环》和《特里斯坦与伊索尔德》展现了前所未有的音乐创新，深刻影响了后世的音乐发展。瓦格纳还通过拜罗伊特音乐节建立了独特的艺术传承体系，使他的艺术理念得以完整呈现。他的音乐不仅具有艺术价值，更承载了深刻的哲学思考，体现了人类精神追求的崇高境界。
supporter.en: Supporters view Wagner as a pioneer in musical theater revolution who broke free from traditional opera constraints, creating the concept of Gesamtkunstwerk (total work of art) that perfectly fused music, poetry, drama, and visual arts. His works like 'The Ring of the Nibelung' and 'Tristan and Isolde' demonstrated unprecedented musical innovation, profoundly influencing subsequent musical development. Wagner also established a unique artistic传承 system through the Bayreuth Festival, allowing his artistic concepts to be fully presented. His music not only possesses artistic value but also carries profound philosophical thought, embodying the sublime realm of human spiritual pursuit.

critic.zh: 批评者指出瓦格纳的作品存在明显的政治和种族偏见，尤其是他的反犹主义思想对后世产生了负面影响。他的音乐虽然创新，但也因其复杂性和长度而难以被大众接受。瓦格纳的个人生活也充满争议，包括多次婚外情和挥霍无度的生活方式。此外，他的作品曾被纳粹政权利用，成为宣传工具，这使他的遗产蒙上了阴影。批评者认为，瓦格纳的艺术成就不应掩盖其道德缺陷和思想上的局限性，他的作品需要被批判性地接受和理解。
critic.en: Critics point out that Wagner's works contain evident political and racial prejudices, particularly his anti-Semitic ideas which had negative impacts on later generations. While his music was innovative, its complexity and length made it difficult for general audiences to accept. Wagner's personal life was also controversial, including multiple extramarital affairs and extravagant lifestyle. Furthermore, his works were appropriated by the Nazi regime as propaganda tools, casting a shadow over his legacy. Critics argue that Wagner's artistic achievements should not overshadow his moral flaws and ideological limitations, and his works need to be received and understood critically.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，瓦格纳被定义为一位具有革命性影响力的作曲家和戏剧理论家。他的音乐创新，如'主导动机'技巧和半音和声体系，彻底改变了西方音乐的发展轨迹。拜罗伊特音乐节成为独特的文化现象，影响深远。瓦格纳的作品不仅在音乐领域产生影响，还渗透到文学、哲学和电影等艺术形式中。同时，他的政治立场和个人争议也成为学术研究的重要课题。在流行文化中，瓦格纳的形象复杂而矛盾，既是艺术天才，也是争议人物，这种双重性使他成为西方文化史上最具魅力和争议的人物之一。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Wagner is defined as a revolutionary composer and dramatic theorist with profound influence. His musical innovations, such as the leitmotif technique and chromatic harmonic system, fundamentally altered the trajectory of Western music development. The Bayreuth Festival became a unique cultural phenomenon with far-reaching influence. Wagner's works not only impacted music but also permeated other art forms like literature, philosophy, and film. Meanwhile, his political stance and personal controversies have become important subjects of academic research. In popular culture, Wagner's image is complex and contradictory—both artistic genius and controversial figure—making him one of the most fascinating and controversial figures in Western cultural history.

self.zh: 音乐应该成为未来诗歌的仆人，诗歌应该成为未来生活的仆人。
self.en: Music should become the servant of future poetry, poetry should become the servant of future life.

others.zh: 瓦格纳的音乐是如此丰富，以至于它包含了整个宇宙。
others.en: Wagner's music is so rich that it contains the whole universe.
